subject: Playback: Dedicated GPU needs & next steps (QVista)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@qvista.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today’s call

Hi Samantha —

Great to speak earlier. Thanks for walking us through the QVista inference workflow and the immediate constraints around cost predictability and data isolation. I wanted to capture the key points we heard and the proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please edit/correct where needed.

Summary of pain and goals
- Primary pain: production inference cost volatility when training and serving custom LLMs; spikes during nightly fine-tune and batch re-ranking jobs.
- Security: must run in an isolated environment (VPC, no multi-tenant co-location) and meet audit log requirements for SOC-style review.
- Latency: real-time ranking path needs predictable p99 latency and <120ms target for 512-token runs.
- Scale: baseline steady-state ~4 concurrent model instances; burst to ~8–10 during training windows or campaign runs.
- Data residency: must remain in us-east region.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Dedicated pool: reserved GPU capacity equivalent to 4x A100-80GB (we’ll show exact SKU/VM mapping) with ability to burst to 8 units for scheduled campaigns.
- Network isolation: private VPC deployment, customer-managed peering, and optional customer KMS integration for keys.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime for the dedicated pool; p99 generation latency target configurable, defaulting to the 120ms goal for the realtime path.
- Reliability play: canary rollout + automatic fallback to a hosted compatible model if pool capacity is transiently unavailable.
- Observability: per-token cost, latency histograms, token-level tracing for the ranking route, and audit logs retained for 13 months (can extend).

Open questions we noted
1) Procurement timeline and PO cadence (Samantha / procurement@qvista.ai)
2) Exact GPU SKU preference (NVIDIA A100 vs next-gen Ampere/Xavier mapping) and whether QVista prefers on-prem or our private cloud region.
3) Confirmation on retention window for logs and any regulatory constraints beyond 13 months.

Next steps and owners
- Connor (me): send an initial MAP (mutual action plan) + pricing matrix by EOD tomorrow (Aug 12). [ACTION: send MAP & pricing]
- Rishi (SE): run a short benchmark with QVista sample payloads (we discussed 3 representative prompts) and share p95/p99 numbers within 48 hours. [ACTION: benchmark]
- Samantha / Procurement: share procurement cadence and preferred contract start date. [ACTION: confirm procurement timeline]

Attachments: I’ll attach a draft Mutual Action Plan and a preliminary pricing workbook in my next email.

Thanks again — felt like a productive start.

—Connor O'Brien

Connor —

Thanks for this clear write-up — this captures the discussion well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement: we typically need 2–3 weeks lead time for PO approvals for new vendors; I’ll check with procurement on whether we can expedite for pilot capacity.
- Audit logs: SOC-style logs are mandatory, and we’ll need a diagram of what’s captured (API calls, token-level traces, user identifiers). 13 months is likely fine but I will confirm.
- GPU SKU: preference is A100-80GB catalog for compatibility with our current quantization pipelines; if you propose an alternate SKU, please call out performance delta.

Two asks: can you include a sample SOW language around network isolation and a short note on how rollbacks/fallbacks are handled during canary? Also, if there’s an acceptable benchmark script or dataset format we should prepare for Rishi, point us to it.

I’ll loop in procurement once we have pricing and the MAP.

Best,
Samantha

Hi Samantha / Connor —

Quick technical addendum based on our call and Samantha’s notes:

Benchmarking guidance
- If you can provide a small representative sample (3–5 inference workloads) in JSONL with the following fields we can run an apples-to-apples test: prompt, max_tokens, batch_size (typical 1–4), and a sample KV cache hit pattern if available.
- We’ll return p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/sec), and GPU memory breakdown for each run.

Model compatibility and quantization
- Our runtime supports FP16 and int8 quantized variants; for large custom LLMs we recommend a mixed approach: use int8 for background batch rerank jobs and FP16 for the realtime ranking route to meet strict latency SLOs.
- KV cache warm starts: suggest a short warm-up window (5–10 requests per model instance) to reach steady-state latency.

Isolation and operations
- Network isolation: we’ll provide a VPC deployment guide and an SOW clause for single-tenant enforcement.
- Rollbacks: canary traffic is shadowed to the new pool and promoted only after p99/p95 thresholds are met for 24 hours; automatic fallback policy will route to hosted compatible model if errors exceed threshold.

I’ll start a benchmark run once we receive the sample JSONL. Happy to hop on a 30-minute technical sync if you want to walk the dataset through.

—Rishi Malhotra
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
